fields.note: Abdul Hamid narrates the crowded prayer between pillars and Anas withdrawal with his own statement about avoiding it in the Messenger period. The crowd-cause parenthesis is narrative causation and stays; English pillars is only a lexical translation. Do not turn Anas statement into direct Prophet speech.
The full Urdu independently supplies the crowd-caused push, between-pillars prayer and Anas own retrospective statement. The cause parenthesis stays. No additional commentary appears.

The source-named Bara/Bare states his own preference to stand on the Prophet right while praying behind him. Right in English parentheses merely repeats दाएं and is context; the actual preference is not the Prophet command.
Bara own finite preference is completely supplied. No English gloss occurs in Urdu, so all its words remain report text.

Zirr reports eating suhur with Hudhayfa, going to the mosque, two sunnah rakats, and a short interval before prayer. This is an actual historical practice report; no Prophet actor or directive is named.
Zirr/Hudhayfa meal and mosque sequence are finite historical content. Preserve the very short interval exactly without inventing a time or Prophetic authority.

Abu Atiyya reports the visit with Masruq, the two Companions contrasting practices, Aisha question, Ibn Masud identification and her Prophet-practice answer. The but connector expresses the actual contrast and stays. The second man is unnamed in this occurrence.

The full own Urdu dialogue supplies the good-deed qualification and contrast and Aisha Prophet-practice answer. Preserve present-tense source wording; do not harmonize it with Hindi or import the later Abu Musa identity.

The complete Abu Atiyya/Masruq/Aisha dialogue supplies Ibn Masud identity and Prophet practice. The final whole parenthetic clause independently states the other man was Abu Musa Ashari. Retain as a distinct historical identification statement with unnamed commenting voice, not automatically Aisha speech.

The full Urdu independently supplies the main dialogue and a finite final Abu Musa identification. It belongs to this account but has no expressly named final speaker; retain it separately in the same family with that qualification.

Read the entire Arabic chain and conversation. Its final والآخر أبو موسى is an actual nominal identification after Aisha answer. The final commenting voice is not explicitly supplied, so do not assign it to Aisha or the Prophet.

The entire English dialogue is supplied with malformed punctuation and a final And the other was Abu Musa. Preserve all words and distinguish that final narrative statement from Aisha quoted answer; no quote repair or guessed voice.
Read the complete Roman Urdu independently. The final full parenthetical identification is finite narrative content, separate from the Aisha dialogue, with no express speaker attached to it.
Aisha reports greatest fasting in Shaban and approximately its entirety. The parenthetic approximately is a necessary extent qualification and cannot be dropped.
The own Urdu explicitly limits almost-all Shaban by تقریباً. Retain that approximation and Aisha report rather than an absolute full-month assertion.

Aisha says she does not know of whole-Quran-in-one-night, whole-night vigil until morning or a whole non-Ramadan month fast. Her epistemic limit is essential; retain whole wording as her report, not a universal prohibition or Prophet speech.
The entire Urdu has the same actually read epistemic I-do-not-know scope and three clauses. No standalone Quran quote or verse locator occurs; all text remains.
Abu Umama directly asks for a command and receives the fasting reply. Worship is explicit comparison domain, and all words are supplied dialogue.
The full dialogue includes عبادت as the comparison domain in parentheses; retain it so nothing-equals does not become unrestricted. The terminal Urdu numeral/footnote glyph is apparatus, not speech.
Abu Umama Bahili asks for beneficial instruction and receives the fasting reply with worship comparison. Whole field is dialogue.
The parenthetic عبادت restricts comparison to worship and remains part of this supplied reply. There is no terminal footnote marker to remove.
Two actual requests and replies occur, with first like-this and then equal wording. Keep the repetition and both clauses; do not compress into one response.
The actual dialogue repeats twice. Parenthetic عمل supplies the first comparison domain and پھر establishes the second request recurrence; both are material report scope, not glossary apparatus.
